facts.statement: The bones of Eoraptor were first discovered in 1991 by paleontologists Ricardo Martínez and Paul Sereno.
facts.quote: The bones of this primitive dinosaur were first discovered in 1991, by University of San Juan paleontologist Ricardo Martínez and Paul Sereno

facts.statement: The genus Eoraptor was formally described and named in 1993 by Paul Sereno, Catherine Forster, Raymond R. Rogers, and Alfredo M. Monetta.
facts.quote: The genus Eoraptor was described and named by Paul Sereno, Catherine Forster, Raymond R. Rogers, and Alfredo M. Monetta in 1993.

facts.statement: Eoraptor is a small, lightly built basal sauropodomorph dinosaur.
facts.quote: Eoraptor () is a genus of small, lightly built, basal sauropodomorph dinosaur.

facts.statement: Known specimens of Eoraptor measure 1.2 to 1.3 meters in length and weigh around or less than 10 kilograms.
facts.quote: Eoraptor was a small dinosaur, with the known specimens measuring 1.2 - 1.3 m in length, and weighing around or less than 10 kg.

facts.statement: Eoraptor ran digitigrade and stood upright on its hind legs.
facts.quote: It ran digitigrade, and upright on its hind legs.

facts.statement: Eoraptor had forelimbs only half the length of its hindlimbs, indicating it was bipedal.
facts.quote: Its forelimbs are only half the length of its hindlimbs, suggesting that it was bipedal.

facts.statement: All of Eoraptor's long bones have hollow shafts.
facts.quote: All of its long bones have hollow shafts.

facts.statement: Eoraptor had five digits on each hand, with the three longest ending in large claws likely used for handling prey.
facts.quote: Eoraptor had five digits on each 'hand', the three longest of which ended in large claws and were presumably used to handle prey.

facts.statement: Eoraptor possessed multiple tooth shapes, suggesting it was an omnivore.
facts.quote: Eoraptor had multiple tooth shapes, which suggests that it was omnivorous.

facts.statement: Eoraptor is thought to have been an omnivore, despite having dentition similar to the carnivorous Buriolestes.
facts.quote: Eoraptor is thought to have been an omnivore, although its dentition is quite similar to that of Buriolestes, which is considered carnivorous.

facts.statement: Eoraptor was a swift sprinter that used claws and teeth to tear apart prey after catching it.
facts.quote: It was a swift sprinter and, upon catching its prey, it would use claws and teeth to tear the prey apart.

facts.statement: Unlike later carnivorous dinosaurs, Eoraptor lacked a sliding joint in its lower jaw, limiting its ability to hold large prey.
facts.quote: Unlike later carnivorous dinosaurs, it lacked a sliding joint at the articulation of the lower jaw, with which to hold large prey.

facts.statement: Eoraptor had heterodont dentition featuring serrated, recurved teeth in the upper jaw and leaf-shaped teeth in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: The heterodont dentition of Eoraptor consists of both serrated, recurved teeth in the upper jaw, like the teeth of theropods, and leaf-shaped teeth in the lower jaw, like the teeth of basal sauropodomorphs.

facts.statement: The classification of Eoraptor has been unstable, with opinions varying between it being a basal saurischian or a basal theropod.
facts.quote: The precise placement of Eoraptor within Dinosauria has been unstable, with opinion often varying between a basal saurischian and a basal theropod.

facts.statement: The name Eoraptor means 'dawn plunderer', referencing its primitive nature and presumed carnivorous habits with a grasping hand.
facts.quote: The name is derived from the Greek word eós () meaning 'dawn', a reference to its primitive nature, and the Latin word meaning 'plunderer', a reference to its presumed carnivorous nature and its grasping hand.

facts.statement: The species name lunensis refers to the 'Valley of the Moon' where the fossils were found, named for its arid, lunar-like appearance.
facts.quote: The specific name lunensis is derived from the Latin words luna ('moon') and the suffix ('inhabitant'), a reference to its place of discovery: the Valle de la Luna ('Valley of the Moon'), so named for its arid, otherworldly appearance evocative of a lunar landscape.

facts.statement: Paul Sereno and colleagues observed in 2013 that Eoraptor's lower jaw had a mid-mandibular joint.
facts.quote: Paul Sereno et al. (2013) observed that the lower jaw had a mid-mandibular joint.

facts.statement: The femur of the holotype Eoraptor measures 152 mm and the tibia 157 mm, suggesting it was a fast runner.
facts.quote: The femur of the holotype specimen PVSJ 512 is 152 mm, and the tibia is 157 mm, suggesting that it was a fast runner.

facts.statement: Scientists believe the fourth and fifth digits of Eoraptor were too small to be useful for hunting.
facts.quote: Scientists have surmised that the fourth and fifth digits were too tiny to be of any use in hunting.

facts.statement: Eoraptor's ilium is supported by three sacral vertebrae, an atypical feature compared to the two sacrals found in basal sauropodomorphs and coeval Herrerasaurus.
facts.quote: The ilium is supported by three sacral vertebrae (atypical of the plesiomorphic two sacrals of basal sauropodomorphs), unlike that of the coeval Herrerasaurus which is supported by only two sacrals, a basal trait.

facts.statement: Eoraptor had a dental formula of 4 teeth in the premaxilla and 18 in the maxilla, similar to that of Herrerasaurus.
facts.quote: Eoraptor had 4 teeth in the premaxilla and 18 teeth in the maxilla, a dental formula not dissimilar to that of Herrerasaurus.

facts.statement: Eoraptor lived in the Late Triassic in a warm, humid floodplain forest with seasonal heavy rainfall.
facts.quote: During the Late Triassic period, the Ischigualasto Formation was a volcanically active floodplain covered by forests, with a warm and humid climate, but subject to seasonal variations including strong rainfall.

facts.statement: Dinosaur fossils, including Eoraptor, make up only about 6% of the total fossil sample from the Ischigualasto Formation.
facts.quote: Dinosaur fossils, including those of Eoraptor only represent approximately 6% of the total sample that has been recovered from the Ischigualasto Formation

facts.statement: An adult Eoraptor was about 1 meter long, 30 centimeters tall, and weighed approximately 10 kilograms.

facts.statement: Its legs were adapted for speed and had four toes.

facts.quote: El fémur del holotipo, el espécimen PVSJ 512 es de 152 milímetros, y la tibia es de 157 milímetros

facts.statement: Eoraptor had five digits on each hand, with the three longest ending in large claws.

facts.statement: The ilium is supported by three sacral vertebrae, unlike Herrerasaurus which has only two, a basal trait.
facts.quote: El ilion es soportado por tres vértebras sacras, a diferencia de la de Herrerasaurus, que es sostenida por solo dos, un rasgo basal

facts.statement: Eoraptor had hollow vertebral centra, a feature present in some of its ancestors.
facts.quote: Eoraptor tenía centros vertebrales huecos, una característica presente en algunos de sus ancestros

facts.statement: Eoraptor was a small carnivore with sharp teeth and claws indicating an active lifestyle.
facts.quote: Eoraptor fue un carnívoro pequeño. Sus dientes y garras filosas demuestran un estilo de vida activo

facts.statement: Eoraptor likely fed on reptiles, small mammals, and insects.

facts.statement: Bonaparte interpreted the relatively large eye orbit as a juvenile trait in 1996.
facts.quote: Bonaparte en 1996 interpretó la órbita ocular relativamente grande del cráneo como un rasgo juvenil

facts.statement: Ronald Tykoski agreed in 2005 that certain skull features suggested the holotype was juvenile.
facts.quote: Ronald Tykoski estuvo de acuerdo en 2005 y sugirió que ciertas características del cráneo del espécimen tipo sugerían que era joven

facts.statement: Paul Sereno and colleagues interpreted Eoraptor as an adult in 1993 based on vertebral suture closure and partial scapulocoracoid fusion.
facts.quote: Paul Sereno et al. en 1993, interpretaron de que Eoraptor era un espécimen adulto basado en el cierre de las suturas en la columna vertebral y la fusión parcial del escapulocoracoide

facts.statement: The generic name Eoraptor combines the Greek word 'Eo' meaning early and the Latin 'raptor' meaning thief.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico de la combinación de las palabras en griego Eo ηως que significa temprano y de la latina raptor, ladrón

facts.statement: The species name lunensis derives from the Latin 'luna' meaning moon and the suffix '-ensis' meaning inhabitant.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, lunensis se deriva de las palabras latinas luna que significa "luna", y el sufijo ~ ensis, que significa "habitante"

facts.statement: Scientists began analyzing the bones of this dinosaur in 1993, dating it to 228 million years ago.
facts.quote: Los científicos iniciaron una serie de revisiones y análisis de los huesos de este dinosaurio en 1993, estableciendo una datación que lo sitúa hace 228 millones de años.

facts.statement: Absolute dating of the rock layers allows Eoraptor to be placed among the oldest known dinosaurs.
facts.quote: El contar con una datación absoluta de los estratos en los que se encontró Eoraptor permite ubicarlo entre los dinosaurios más antiguos conocidos.

facts.statement: Unlike later carnivores, Eoraptor lacked a sliding joint in the lower jaw that would allow it to hold large prey.
facts.quote: A diferencia de los carnívoros posteriores, carecía una articulación deslizante en la articulación de la mandíbula inferior, con la cual podía sostener una presa grande.

facts.statement: Only some of its teeth were curved and sharp, differing from those of later predators.
facts.quote: Además, solamente algunos de sus dientes estaban curvados y afilados, diferenciándose de los de un predador posterior.

facts.statement: Eoraptor belonged to an important group of dinosaurs called saurischians.
facts.quote: Eoraptor perteneció a un grupo importante de dinosaurios llamados los saurisquios.

facts.statement: Its hip structures are similar to those of the modern lizard.
facts.quote: Sus estructuras de la cadera son similares a la del lagarto moderno.

facts.statement: The fact that Eoraptor's skull possessed some herbivore teeth and five fully developed fingers has led scientists to place it as more primitive than even Herrerasaurus.
facts.quote: El hecho que el cráneo de Eoraptor poseyera algunos dientes del herbívoro y cinco dedos completamente desarrollados ha llevado a científicos a colocar Eoraptor como más primitivo que incluso Herrerasaurus.

facts.statement: In 1993, Paul Sereno and his colleagues described and named Eoraptor and determined it was one of the first dinosaurs.
facts.quote: En 1993, Paul Sereno y sus colegas describieron y nombraron a Eoraptor y determinaron que era uno de los primeros dinosaurios.

facts.statement: Its jaws possessed very varied teeth, some sharp for cutting meat like carnosaurs, others curved for crushing plants like sauropods, and some leaf-shaped for stripping branches like ornithopods, suggesting it may have been an omnivore.
facts.quote: Sus mandíbulas poseían dientes muy variados, algunos afilados diseñados para cortar carne como los de los carnosaurios, otros curvados diseñados para triturar hierbas y plantas como los de los saurópodos y algunos en forma de hoja diseñados para arrancar ramas y agujas como los de los ornitópodos, por lo que se cree que pudo haber sido un omnívoro.

facts.statement: One possibility is that it is the most basal theropod, outside a clade containing herrerasaurids and Avetheropoda, or as a sister group to the clade including sauropodomorphs and theropods, Eusaurischia.
facts.quote: Una posibilidad es que sea el terópodo más basal, fuera de un clado que contiene a los herrerasáuridos y los Avepoda, o como un grupo hermano del clado que incluye a los sauropodomorfos y terópodos, Eusaurischia.

facts.statement: When first described by Sereno and Forster in 1993, it was considered a theropod based on its "functionally three-fingered hand" and other anatomical features.
facts.quote: Cuando fue descrito por primera vez por Sereno y Forster en 1993, fue considerado como un terópodo, basado en su "mano funcionalmente tridáctila" y otras características anatómicas.

facts.statement: In 2011, a study by Hans-Dieter Sues, Sterling J. Nesbitt, David S. Berman, and Amy C. Henrici concluded that there were now enough fossil evidence to confidently classify Eoraptor as a theropod.
facts.quote: En 2011, un estudio realizado por Hans-Dieter Sues, Sterling J. Nesbitt , David S. Berman y Amy C. Henrici con una descripción de Daemonosaurus, también concluyó lo mismo y dijo que ahora hay suficientes pruebas fósiles para clasificar con confianza a Eoraptor como un terópodo.

facts.statement: In 2011, Martínez et al., the team that described Eodromaeus, discovered that Eoraptor is a basal sauropodomorph with group characteristics.
facts.quote: En 2011, Martínez et al., el equipo que describió a Eodromaeus, descubrió que Eoraptor es un sauropodomorfo basal, con características del grupo.

facts.statement: Michael Benton expressed hesitation regarding this, stating that removing Eoraptor from Theropoda and placing it in Sauropodomorpha is "a big change."
facts.quote: Michael Benton expresó su vacilación al respecto, y afirmó que es "un gran cambio" eliminar a Eoraptor de Theropoda y luego colocarlo en Sauropodomorpha.

facts.statement: A later study by Apaldetti, Martínez, Alcober, and Pol, published in 2011, revealed that Eoraptor is a saurischian close to sauropodomorphs and theropods, though it could not resolve which of the two branches it would be classified in, if that is the case.
facts.quote: Un estudio posterior realizado por Apaldetti, Martínez, Alcober y Pol, publicado en 2011, reveló que Eoraptor es un saurisquio cercano a los sauropodomorfos y terópodos, aunque no pudo resolver en cuál de las dos ramas se clasificaría, si es que ese es el caso.

facts.statement: Sereno et al. in 2011 redesigned the holotype skeleton and concluded that Eoraptor was not a theropod but a basal sauropodomorph, consistent with the earlier observation made by Martínez et al. in 2011.
facts.quote: Sereno et al. en 201) rediseñaron el esqueleto holotipo y concluyeron que Eoraptor no era un terópodo, sino un sauropodomorfo basal, consistente con la observación anterior hecha por Martínez et al. en 2011.

facts.statement: A major phylogenetic analysis of early dinosaurs conducted by Matthew Baron, David Norman, and Paul Barrett in 2017 found Eoraptor as the first divergent member of Theropoda, within the larger clade Ornithoscelida.
facts.quote: Un gran análisis filogenético de los primeros dinosaurios realizado por Matthew Baron, David Norman y Paul Barrett en 2017 encontró a Eoraptor como el primer miembro divergente de Theropoda, dentro del clado más grande Ornithoscelida.
